title: HUD Compliance Matrix for Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases
content:
This matrix sets out, plan by plan, the HUD settings that govern when a Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases case is called due. The figures and settings are those of each case plan.

| Case plan | HUD approval required before the loan is called due | HUD notified or approval requested within | Unrepaid property-charge advances above which HUD approval is requested | Cure period a default notice gives before approval is requested |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Death of Last Surviving Borrower | no | 30 calendar days | 0.00 (not a property charge case) | 0 (not a default case) |
| Sale or Title Transfer | no | 30 calendar days | 0.00 (not a property charge case) | 0 (not a default case) |
| Extended Health-Care Absence | yes | 30 calendar days | 0.00 (not a property charge case) | 0 (not a default case) |
| Principal Residence Change | yes | 30 calendar days | 0.00 (not a property charge case) | 0 (not a default case) |
| Property Charge Default | yes | 30 calendar days | 2000.00 dollars | 30 calendar days |
| Property Condition Default | yes | 30 calendar days | 0.00 (not a property charge case) | 60 calendar days |

The HUD notice period is counted from the date the servicer learns of the event.

**HUD notification, approval and extension steps on a Cedarline Summit loan:** under all six plans these steps do not apply to a Summit loan.

## Points of judgement

- **Approval or notification?** A plan marked "no" in the approval column (death, sale or transfer) involves notifying HUD. A plan marked "yes" involves asking HUD for approval to call the loan due.
- **Property charge threshold, both sides:** under the Property Charge Default plan the figure is 2000.00 dollars. Hypothetical unrepaid advances of 2000.01 dollars are above it; advances of exactly 2000.00 dollars are not.
- **Default notice cure period:** 30 calendar days for a property charge default and 60 calendar days for a property condition default. The other four plans give none.
